risk_review.notes: The exact generic defect-insertion interface is reused only for model-bound codimension-two insertion data. The item separates GMN and KT metric/period conventions, leaves the physical charge map model-supplied, and does not identify geometric webs with physical states or numerical indices.

citations.quote: A geometric WKB network is generated from the maximal such trajectories issuing from branch points and from the local junction rule: when compatible $ij$- and $jk$-trajectories meet, an $ik$-trajectory may issue from their joint.

A **finite web** is a finite connected metric ribbon graph: each edge has positive finite length and a cyclic order at each vertex; each internal vertex is trivalent and maps to a network joint, and each external univalent vertex maps to a branch point.
For a closed web, the chosen sheet-lift rule joins its oriented sheetwise edge lifts into a cycle $\gamma_{\rm geom}\in\Gamma_{\rm geom}$.

The physical charge group $\Gamma_{\mathcal T}$ is a model-specified quotient of a subgroup $\Gamma_0\le\Gamma_{\rm geom}$, supplied with a surjective quotient map $\rho:\Gamma_0\to\Gamma_{\mathcal T}$; it is not identified with all of $H_1(\widetilde\Sigma;\mathbb Z)$ by notation alone.

derivations.claim: In the Eisenstein basis, B-A=(2/3,1/3)=(2+omega)/3 has flat length 1/sqrt(3), KT slope pi/6, sheet-difference phase 0 for the selected pair, and determinant Delta=3.

The open segment contains no branch value and no self-identification under the torus lattice or deck quotient, so its projection is an embedded regular trajectory with both orientations in the initial network.

The one-edge graph is isometric in the KT metric; the same sheet-pair edge has GMN length 1, which would give normalized mass 1/pi under the GMN string convention, without assigning a physical mass to this geometric example.
The closed cycle p-tau(p) has integral (1-omega)(2+omega)/3=1, hence is nonzero in H_1 because lambda is closed; this remains a geometric charge only.

Example: the construction is one finite edge with two univalent branch-point vertices; its length is 1/sqrt(3) in the KT cover metric and 1 in the GMN sheet-difference metric.
Example: The endpoints are allowed branch values; the open edge contains no branch value and the calculation is restricted to the source's alpha=1 T3 differential and rational slope (2,1).
Example: The lifted path difference has cancelling endpoint boundary and is an absolute one-cycle; an interface-framed charge would instead be a relative class and is not computed.

ex-qftx-t3-finite-web-index.finite_checks_disposition: This exact finite geometric check verifies one source-normalized T3 web and its geometric period only. It does not establish a physical charge image, state existence, or a numerical bulk, soliton, or framed index.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
For distinct sheets $i,j$, a regular **$ij$-trajectory of Wentzel–Kramers–Brillouin (WKB) phase** $\vartheta_{\rm W}\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$ is a $C^1$ immersed path $z:I\to C\setminus\operatorname{Branch}(\pi)$, for an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, with $\dot z\ne0$ and

$$\operatorname{Im}\!\left(e^{-i\vartheta_{\rm W}}(\lambda^{(i)}-\lambda^{(j)})(\dot z)\right)=0.$$
supplier_excerpts.relevant_hypotheses_and_conventions: The path avoids branch values and punctures; the sheet-difference phase is distinct from the KT flat-slope phase and from the framed-interface phase.
